copy.tl: Ang quartz ay isa sa pinakakaraniwang mineral sa Earth! Sa totoo lang, karamihan ng puting buhangin sa beach ay maliliit na butil ng quartz.
copy.bis: Ang quartz usa sa labing kasagaran nga mineral sa Earth! Sa tinuud, kadaghanan sa puti nga balas sa baybayon gagmay nga lugas sa quartz.

copy.en:
How does quicksand form?

It happens when water seeps up through sand! The sand loses its firmness and turns soft and slippery, just like mud.
copy.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang quicksand?

Nangyayari ito kapag umaapaw ang tubig sa ilalim ng buhangin! Nawawalan ito ng tigas at nagiging malambot at madulas na parang putik.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagporma ang quicksand?

Mahitabo kini kung moawas ang tubig gikan sa ilalom sa balas! Mawad-an kini og katig-a ug mahimong humok ug danlog sama sa lapok.

copy.en: Radiant energy is energy that travels through space as waves, like sunlight, X-rays, and the heat from a glowing light bulb.
copy.tl: Ang radiant energy ay energy na naglalakbay sa espasyo bilang mga alon, tulad ng sikat ng araw, X-rays, at init mula sa nagliliwanag na bombilya.
copy.bis: Ang radiant energy mao ang energy nga mobiyahe sa espasyo isip mga balod, sama sa kahayag sa adlaw, X-rays, ug kainit gikan sa nagdan-ag nga bombilya.

copy.tl: Sa radiation, naglalakbay ang init bilang invisible rays kahit walang hangin, tulad ng init ng araw na umaabot sa Earth!
copy.bis: Sa radiation, nagbiyahe ang kainit isip invisible rays bisan walay hangin, sama sa kainit sa adlaw nga moabot sa Earth!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In radiation, heat travels as invisible waves!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation

copy.en: In radiation, heat travels as invisible waves! This is why the sun's warmth reaches us even with no air between us and the sun.
copy.tl: Sa radiation, naglalakbay ang init bilang mga di-nakikitang alon! Kaya naaabot tayo ng init ng araw kahit walang hangin sa pagitan natin.
copy.bis: Sa radyasyon, mobiyahe ang init isip dili makita nga mga balod! Mao nga makaabot ang init sa adlaw kanato bisan walay hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In radiation, heat travels as rays or waves and needs no material in between!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the mechanism of radiation (no medium needed) but does not identify any advantageous or disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, or radiation as required by the competency. It provides background on radiation only, not the specific skill of identifying pros/cons.

copy.en:
How does heat travel through empty space?

In radiation, heat travels as rays or waves and needs no material in between! That's why heat can travel through the empty vacuum of space.
copy.tl:
Paano lumalakbay ang init sa walang-hangin na kalawakan?

Sa radiation, naglalakbay ang init sa anyo ng sinag (waves) at hindi nangangailangan ng anumang bagay sa pagitan! Kaya kayang dumaan ng init kahit sa walang-hangin na kalawakan.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglabay sa init sa walay-hangin nga kawanangan?

Sa radiation, ang init molabay isip silaw (waves) ug wala manginahanglan og bisan unsang butang sa tunga! Busa makaagi ang init bisan sa walay-hangin nga kawanangan.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that radio waves (a type of EMR) can travel through empty space, which touches on one aspect of the competency (travel through space). copy.en:
Can radio waves travel through empty space?

Yes! Unlike sound that needs air or water, radio waves move right through empty space. This lets us talk to satellites and astronauts floating up there!
copy.tl:
Nakakadaan ba ang radio waves sa walang laman na espasyo?

Oo! Hindi tulad ng tunog na kailangan ng hangin o tubig, dumaan ang radio waves sa walang laman na espasyo. Kaya nakakapag-talk tayo sa mga satellite at astronaut!
copy.bis:
Makaagi ba ang radio waves sa walay sulod nga espasyo?

Oo! Dili sama sa tingog nga nagkinahanglan og hangin o tubig, makalihok ang radio waves bisan walay sulod nga espasyo. Mao nga makapahimamat ta sa mga satellite ug astronaut!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Radio, Wi-Fi, and phone signals travel at the speed of light!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that radio, Wi-Fi, and phone signals travel at the speed of light, which is a property of electromagnetic radiation, but it does not describe EMR as energy created by vibrations of electrically charged particles or as transverse waves. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency's specific content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Radio, Wi-Fi, and phone signals travel at the speed of light!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify practical applications of electromagnetic radiation, such as radio waves used in telecommunications, and x-rays and gamma rays in medicine
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions radio signals, which are an example of electromagnetic radiation used in telecommunications, but it does not identify practical applications of EMR such as radio waves in telecommunications or x-rays/gamma rays in medicine. It only notes their speed, not their uses.

copy.en: Radio, Wi-Fi, and phone signals travel at the speed of light! It's the fastest speed ever, so they arrive almost instantly, even from far away.
copy.tl: Ang radio, Wi-Fi, at phone signals ay naglalakbay sa speed of light! Ito ang pinakamabilis, kaya halos walang delay ang pagdating kahit malayo.
copy.bis: Ang radio, Wi-Fi, ug phone signals mobiyahe sa speed of light! Kini ang pinakakusog, mao nga halos walay delay ang pag-abot bisan layo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: two protons and two neutrons stuck together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions protons and neutrons but does not differentiate subatomic particles by symbol, mass, charge, or location. It only describes an alpha particle as a helium nucleus, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Losing two protons turns the atom into a new element
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on protons determining element identity, which is part of G8-M-4b, but it does not describe pure substances, fixed chemical composition, or elements/compounds. The alpha-decay context is not aligned with the competency's instructional goal.

copy.en: In alpha decay, the nucleus shoots out an 'alpha particle' — two protons and two neutrons stuck together (a helium nucleus!). Losing two protons turns the atom into a new element.
copy.tl: Sa alpha decay, naglalabas ang nucleus ng 'alpha particle' — dalawang proton at dalawang neutron na magkakasama (isang helium nucleus!). Nawalan ng dalawang proton, kaya nagiging ibang element na ang atomo.
copy.bis: Sa alpha decay, mogawas ang nucleus og 'alpha particle' — duha ka proton ug duha ka neutron nga magdugtong (usa ka helium nucleus!). Nawad-an og duha ka proton, mao nga laing element na ang atomo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a 'gamma ray' — a super powerful invisible light
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes gamma rays as a type of invisible light carrying extra energy from the nucleus. It does not compare wavelengths or frequencies of different electromagnetic waves, nor does it mention any other EM wave types. Thus it does not directly support the competency's comparison skill.

copy.en:
What is gamma decay?

No protons or neutrons are lost! The nucleus just releases extra energy as a 'gamma ray' — a super powerful invisible light. It often happens right after alpha or beta decay.
copy.tl:
Ano ang gamma decay?

Walang nawawalang proton o neutron! Naglalabas lang ang nucleus ng sobrang enerhiya bilang 'gamma ray' — isang napakalakas na hindi nakikitang liwanag. Madalas ito pagkatapos ng alpha o beta decay.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gamma decay?

Walay nawala nga proton o neutron! Mogawas lang ang nucleus og sobra nga enerhiya isip 'gamma ray' — usa ka kusgan kaayo nga dili makita nga kahayag. Kasagaran kini human sa alpha o beta decay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Strong radiation can damage our cells and DNA
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes and discuss some of the factors that cause mutations, such as infectious agents, radiation, and chemicals
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that strong radiation can damage cells and DNA, which is background related to radiation as a mutation-causing factor. However, it does not describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes, nor does it discuss the factors causing mutations in the manner required by the competency. The card is about radiation safety, not about mutations.

copy.en: Strong radiation can damage our cells and DNA, which is why workers wear protective gear! But the small natural radiation around us is perfectly safe.
copy.tl: Ang malakas na radiation ay nakakasisira ng cells at DNA, kaya nagsusuot ng protective gear ang mga trabahador! Pero ang konting natural radiation sa paligid ay ligtas.
copy.bis: Ang kusgan nga radiation makadaot sa cells ug DNA, mao nga nagsul-ob og protective gear ang mga trabahante! Apan ang gamay nga natural radiation luwas ra.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a large group of identical atoms decays at a predictable rate! This helps scientists estimate the age of rocks and fossils.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how relative and absolute dating techniques are used to determine the subdivisions of geologic time
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the underlying principle of radiometric (absolute) dating, but does not describe relative dating techniques, nor how these techniques are used to determine subdivisions of geologic time. It provides background knowledge for absolute dating rather than directly teaching the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This helps scientists estimate the age of rocks and fossils.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how fossils can be used for dating the age of rocks and sediments
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that decay rate helps estimate the age of rocks and fossils, which is the basis of radiometric dating, but it does not describe how fossils themselves are used for dating rocks and sediments. It supports the concept of absolute dating but does not directly teach fossil-based dating methods.

copy.en: We can't predict when one nucleus will decay, but a large group of identical atoms decays at a predictable rate! This helps scientists estimate the age of rocks and fossils.
copy.tl: Hindi mahuhulaan kung kailan masisira ang isang nucleus, pero ang malaking grupo ng parehong atom ay nasisira sa matatantyang bilis! Nagagamit ito sa pagtaya ng edad ng mga bato at fossil.
copy.bis: Dili matag-an kung kanus-a madunot ang usa ka nucleus, apan ang dako nga grupo sa parehong atom madunot sa matagna nga tulin! Magamit kini sa pagbanabana sa edad sa mga bato ug fossil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When protons and neutrons in an atom's nucleus aren't balanced
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions protons and neutrons but does not differentiate them by symbol, mass, charge, or location. It focuses on nuclear stability and radioactive decay, which is not the competency's content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: in an atom's nucleus
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to the nucleus but does not draw or describe the structure of an atom in terms of nucleus and electron shells. It is about radioactive decay, not atomic structure.

copy.en: When protons and neutrons in an atom's nucleus aren't balanced, it becomes 'unstable.' To feel steady again, it releases energy or a particle — this is radioactive decay!
copy.tl: Kapag hindi balanse ang proton at neutron sa nucleus ng atomo, nagiging 'unstable' ito. Para maging matatag, naglalabas ito ng enerhiya o particle — ito ang radioactive decay!
copy.bis: Kung dili balanse ang proton ug neutron sa nucleus sa atomo, kini mahimong 'unstable.' Aron magmalig-on, mogawas kini og enerhiya o particle — mao kini ang radioactive decay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use radiometric dating! Carbon-14 measures things under 50,000 years old, while potassium-argon and uranium-lead are used to date much older rocks!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how relative and absolute dating techniques are used to determine the subdivisions of geologic time
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains absolute dating methods (radiometric dating) and their applicable age ranges, which is background knowledge for understanding absolute dating. However, it does not describe relative dating techniques, nor does it connect these techniques to determining subdivisions of geologic time, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en:
How do scientists measure the age of ancient rocks and fossils?

They use radiometric dating! Carbon-14 measures things under 50,000 years old, while potassium-argon and uranium-lead are used to date much older rocks!
copy.tl:
Paano sinusukat ng mga siyentipiko ang edad ng mga sinaunang bato at fosil?

Ginagamit nila ang radiometric dating! Ang carbon-14 ay para sa mga bagay na mas bata sa 50,000 taon, habang ang potassium-argon at uranium-lead ay para sa mas matandang bato!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsukat sa mga siyentipiko sa edad sa karaang mga bato ug fossil?

Nagamit nila ang radiometric dating! Ang carbon-14 alang sa mga butang ubos sa 50,000 ka tuig, samtang ang potassium-argon ug uranium-lead alang sa mas karaan nga mga bato!

copy.en:
How long does a Rafflesia flower last?

Even though its bud takes so long to grow, the open flower lasts only a few days before turning black and wilting.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal namumulaklak ang Rafflesia?

Kahit matagal lumaki ang buko nito, tumatagal lang ng ilang araw ang bukas na bulaklak bago ito mangitim at malanta.
copy.bis:
Kadugayon mobukhad ang bulak sa Rafflesia?

Bisan dugay motubo ang buko niini, molungtad lang og pila ka adlaw ang abli nga bulak una kini moitom ug malaya.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves only to explain why the Rafflesia bud cannot photosynthesize; it does not teach observing outer plant parts or their role in taking up water and nutrients from the soil.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: Food and water are mentioned as things the bud obtains, but the card does not teach the general concept of basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it has no green leaves!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a parasitic plant's food source, not an adaptation to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. The absence of leaves is not presented as an environmental adaptation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: draws food and water straight from the host vine it grows on
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows one plant taking food and water from another plant, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs in the sense of interdependence.

copy.en:
Why doesn't the Rafflesia bud make its own food?

Because it has no green leaves! Instead, the Rafflesia bud draws food and water straight from the host vine it grows on.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi gumagawa ng sariling pagkain ang buko ng Rafflesia?

Dahil wala itong berdeng dahon! Sa halip, sinisipsip ng buko ng Rafflesia ang pagkain at tubig direkta mula sa baging na sinasakyan nito.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili maghimo og kaugalingong pagkaon ang buko sa Rafflesia?

Kay walay lunhaw nga dahon! Hinuon, gisuyop sa buko sa Rafflesia ang pagkaon ug tubig direkta gikan sa liana nga gisak-an niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rafflesia buds grow better in damp, rainy weather
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a plant preferring damp, rainy conditions, which is a favorable condition, not an adaptation to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rafflesia buds grow better in damp, rainy weather
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rain and moisture as environmental factors affecting a plant, but it does not describe the distinction between biotic and abiotic factors or classify Rafflesia as a biotic factor and rain as an abiotic factor. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rafflesia buds grow better in damp, rainy weather
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a plant depending on rain/moisture from the environment, which is a simple example of dependence on the environment. It is a single example without the explanatory component required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why do Rafflesia buds love rainy forests?

Rafflesia buds grow better in damp, rainy weather, so they often appear inside humid forests.
copy.tl:
Bakit gustong-gusto ng Rafflesia ang maulang gubat?

Mas mabilis lumaki ang buko ng Rafflesia sa mamasa-masa at maulang panahon, kaya madalas itong sumulpot sa mahalumigmig na gubat.
copy.bis:
Nganong gusto kaayo sa Rafflesia ang ulanon nga lasang?

Mas paspas modako ang buko sa Rafflesia sa basa ug ulanon nga panahon, mao nga sagad kini mogula sa umog nga kalasangan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tiny Rafflesia seeds are carried by animals like rats or ants to other vines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Animals carrying seeds is dispersal, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: where a new bud may grow someday
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: Seed-to-bud is one plant stage, not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

copy.en: After it blooms and fruits, tiny Rafflesia seeds are carried by animals like rats or ants to other vines, where a new bud may grow someday.
copy.tl: Matapos mamulaklak at magbunga, dinadala ng mga hayop tulad ng daga o langgam ang maliliit na buto ng Rafflesia papunta sa ibang baging, kung saan maaaring tumubo ang bagong buko balang-araw.
copy.bis: Human mamulak ug mamunga, gidala sa mga mananap sama sa ilaga o hulmigas ang gagmay nga liso sa Rafflesia ngadto sa ubang liana, diin mahimong motubo ang bag-ong buko sa umaabot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Rafflesia arnoldii flower grows to about 1 meter across
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that the flower 'grows' to a certain size, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a concept. It is a specific fact about one plant's size, not instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
How big can the Rafflesia flower grow?

The Rafflesia arnoldii flower grows to about 1 meter across — as wide as a car tire!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalaki ang bulaklak ng Rafflesia?

Ang bulaklak ng Rafflesia arnoldii ay umaabot ng halos 1 metro ang lapad — kasing laki ng gulong ng kotse!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadako ang bulak sa Rafflesia?

Ang bulak sa Rafflesia arnoldii moabot og mga 1 metro ang gilapdon — sama kadako sa ligid sa awto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It can weigh up to 11 kilograms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions the unit 'kilograms' in a factual statement about a flower's weight. It does not teach identification or appropriate use of units in simple science activities, nor does it provide any instructional support for measuring or choosing units.

copy.en:
How heavy can a Rafflesia flower get?

It can weigh up to 11 kilograms — that's one seriously heavy flower!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabigat ang bulaklak ng Rafflesia?

Kaya nitong tumimbang ng hanggang 11 kilo — sobrang bigat para sa isang bulaklak!
copy.bis:
Unsa kabug-at ang bulak sa Rafflesia?

Makaabot kini og kabug-aton nga hangtod 11 ka kilo — grabe kabug-at alang sa usa ka bulak!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its bud slowly grows for many months

copy.en:
How long before a Rafflesia bud blooms?

Its bud slowly grows for many months, looking like a brown cabbage — but once it's ready, the giant flower opens quite suddenly!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal bago bumukad ang Rafflesia?

Dahan-dahang lumalaki ang usbong nito sa loob ng maraming buwan, parang kulay-kayumangging repolyo — pero kapag handa na, biglaang bumubukad ang higanteng bulaklak!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay una mobukhad ang Rafflesia?

Hinay-hinay nga motubo ang usbong niini sulod sa daghang bulan, morag brown nga repolyo — apan kung andam na, kalit ra mobukhad ang dako nga bulak!

copy.en:
How does Rafflesia spread its seeds?

Rafflesia seeds are very tiny and are thought to stick to animals like rats or deer, which carry them to other vines where a new plant can grow.
copy.tl:
Paano kumakalat ang buto ng Rafflesia?

Napakaliit ng buto ng Rafflesia at pinaniniwalaang dumidikit ito sa mga hayop tulad ng daga o usa, na nagdadala nito sa ibang baging kung saan maaaring tumubo ang bagong halaman.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkatag sa binhi sa Rafflesia?

Gagmay kaayo ang binhi sa Rafflesia ug gituohan nga modikit kini sa mga hayop sama sa ilaga o usa, nga modala niini sa ubang liana diin makatubo ang bag-ong tanom.

copy.bis: Nagkalainlain ang ulan sa Pilipinas depende sa dapit! Super madag-ulan ang Baguio City, nga makadawat og labaw sa 4,000 mm sa ulan matag tuig.

How does rain fall from the sky?

Tiny water droplets in a cloud join together until they get heavy enough to fall to the ground as rain!
copy.tl:
Paano bumabagsak ang ulan mula sa langit?

Nagsasama-sama ang maliliit na patak ng tubig sa ulap hanggang sa maging mabigat sila at bumagsak sa lupa bilang ulan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahulog sa ulan gikan sa langit?

Nagtapok ang gagmayng tinulo sa tubig sa panganod hangtod nga mabug-at na sila ug mahulog sa yuta isip ulan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's frontal rain! The cold air pushes the warm air upward, and as it rises, it creates steady, long-lasting rainfall.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a type of weather (frontal rain) and its cause, but does not address observing or recording weather changes over time, nor describing local weather types/patterns as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's frontal rain! The cold air pushes the warm air upward, and as it rises, it creates steady, long-lasting rainfall.

copy.en:
What happens when cold air meets warm air in the sky?

That's frontal rain! The cold air pushes the warm air upward, and as it rises, it creates steady, long-lasting rainfall.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagtagpo ang malamig at mainit na hangin sa kalangitan?

Yan ang frontal rain! Itinutulak ng malamig na hangin ang mainit na hangin pataas, at habang umaakyat ito, nagdudulot ng tuluy-tuloy na ulan.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung magtagbo ang malamig ug mainit nga hangin sa langit?

Mao na ang frontal rain! Ang malamig nga hangin nagtulod sa mainit nga hangin paibabaw, ug samtang mosaka, naghatag og tuluy-tuloy nga ulan.

copy.tl: Ang 1 mm na ulan sa rain gauge ay nangangahulugang lalim na 1 milimetro lang ang tubig sa patag na lupa!
copy.bis: Ang 1 mm nga ulan sa rain gauge nagpasabot nga 1 milimetro ra ka lawom ang tubig sa patag nga yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What does a rain gauge reading of 1 millimeter really mean?

copy.en:
What does a rain gauge reading of 1 millimeter really mean?

It means the rain would form a layer exactly 1 millimeter deep over a flat area — if none of it ran off or evaporated!
copy.tl:
Ano ba ang ibig sabihin ng 1 millimeter na basa sa rain gauge?

Ibig sabihin, lalalim nang 1 millimeter ang ulan sa isang patag na lugar — kung walang umaagos o sumisingaw na tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsay buot ipasabot sa 1 millimeter nga basa sa rain gauge?

Nagpasabot nga ang ulan mahimong layer nga 1 millimeter ang giladmon sa patag nga dapit — kon walay modagayday o moalisngaw nga tubig!

copy.en:
How does PAGASA use rain gauges to keep us safe?

PAGASA tracks how heavy and how much rain falls. When the amount gets very high, they issue a flood warning!
copy.tl:
Paano ginagamit ng PAGASA ang mga rain gauge para sa kaligtasan natin?

Tinitiyak ng PAGASA kung gaano kalakas at kadami ang ulan. Kapag napakarami na, naglalabas sila ng babala sa baha!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paggamit sa PAGASA sa mga rain gauge aron luwas kita?

Gisusi sa PAGASA kung unsa kakusog ug kadaghan ang uwan. Kon hilabihan kadaghan, mopagawas sila og pasidaan sa baha!

copy.bis: Sa panahon sa tag-ulan sa Pilipinas, kadaghanan sa ulan gikan sa habagat (southwest monsoon), nga nagdala sa basa nga hangin gikan sa dagat padulong sa yuta.

copy.en:
What brings super heavy rain to the Philippines?

The monsoon trough, or intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ), is a low-pressure line where winds meet and bring extreme rain!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagdadala ng napakalakas na ulan sa Pilipinas?

Ang monsoon trough, o intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ), ay isang low-pressure line kung saan nagtatagpo ang hangin para magdala ng extreme rain!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagdala og labihan ka kusog nga ulan sa Pilipinas?

Ang monsoon trough, o intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ), usa ka low-pressure line kung diin magtagbo ang hangin aron magdala og extreme rain!

copy.en: When wind pushes clouds up a mountain, they cool and dump rain on the front! By the time air crosses to the other side, it is squeezed dry, creating a dry rain shadow.
copy.tl: Kapag tinutulak ng hangin ang ulap pataas sa bundok, lumalamig ito at umuulan sa harap! Pagdating sa kabilang gilid, ubos na ang basa, kaya tuyo at kung minsan disyerto pa ang likuran, tinatawag itong rain shadow.
copy.bis: Kon itulak sa hangin ang panganod pataas sa bukid, mobugnaw kini ug mo-ulan sa atubangang kilid! Pag-abot sa pikas kilid, nahurot na ang kaumog, maong uga ug usahay disyerto pa ang luyo, nga gitawag og rain shadow.

copy.bis: Ang rainwater sama sa delivery truck, nagdala sa mga mineral gikan sa top layer paubos sa subsoil!

copy.bis: Aron makakita og balangaw, kinahanglan sa imong likod ang adlaw ug sa imong atubangan ang ulan — busa kanunay anaa sa atbang nga bahin sa langit ang balangaw, dili sa kilid sa adlaw!

copy.tl: Sa lahat ng magagandang kulay ng bahaghari, ang pula ang may pinakamahabang wavelength!
copy.bis: Sa tanang nindot nga kolor sa balangaw, ang pula ang adunay pinakataas nga wavelength!

Can you see two rainbows at once?

Yes! The second rainbow is outside, fainter, and has reversed colors because light reflects twice inside the raindrops.
copy.tl:
Pwede bang makakita ng dalawang bahaghari nang sabay?

Oo! Ang pangalawa ay nasa labas, mas malabo, at baligtad ang kulay dahil sumasalamin nang dalawang beses ang liwanag sa loob ng patak.
copy.bis:
Pwede bang makakita og duha ka balangaw nga dungan?

Oo! Ang ikaduha anaa sa gawas, mas hanap, ug balit-ad ang kulay kay mosalamin og kaduha ang kahayag sa sulod sa tulo.

When do we usually see a rainbow in the sky?

A rainbow is an arc of colors that usually appears after rain, while the Sun is still shining brightly!
copy.tl:
Kailan karaniwang nakikita ang bahaghari sa kalangitan?

Ang bahaghari ay isang arko ng mga kulay na karaniwang lumilitaw pagkatapos ng ulan, habang sumisikat pa rin ang Araw!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a kasagaran makita ang balangaw sa langit?

Ang balangaw usa ka arko sa mga kolor nga kasagaran motungha human sa ulan, samtang nagsidlak pa ang Adlaw!

copy.en:
Is a rainbow really a full circle?

Yes! We usually see only the top arch because the ground blocks the lower half. From an airplane, you can sometimes see the whole ring!
copy.tl:
Ang bahaghari ba ay talagang buong bilog?

Oo! Nakikita lang natin ang ibabaw na arko dahil hinaharang ng lupa ang ibabang kalahati. Mula sa eroplano, minsan kitang-kita ang buong singsing!
copy.bis:
Ang balangaw ba tinuod nga tibuok lingin?

Oo! Kasagaran makita lang nato ang ibabaw nga arko kay ang yuta nagsanta sa ubos nga katunga. Gikan sa eroplano, usahay makita ang tibuok singsing!

copy.bis: Mahimo ang bangaw kung mosidlak ang adlaw samtang nag-ulan, ug moagi ang kahayag sa gagmay nga mga tinulo sa tubig!

copy.en: Inside a raindrop, light bends entering (refraction), reflects off the back, and bends again leaving! This separates the colors to form the rainbow.
copy.tl: Sa loob ng patak ng ulan, bumabaluktot ang liwanag pagpasok (refraction), sumasalamin sa likod, at bumabaluktot ulit paglabas! Dito naghihiwalay ang mga kulay.
copy.bis: Sa sulod sa tulo sa ulan, mobaliko ang kahayag pagsulod (refraction), mosalamin sa likod, ug mobaliko pag-usab paggawas! Dinhi mabahin ang mga bulok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Big ones flatten on the bottom like a tiny hamburger bun as they fall through the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the physical shape of raindrops, not the characteristics used to describe weather (e.g., air temperature, wind, humidity, rain as a weather element). It does not directly support identifying weather characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Big ones flatten on the bottom like a tiny hamburger bun as they fall through the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that larger raindrops flatten as they fall, which touches on shape affecting movement, but it does not explore or describe how size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture affect the movement of objects in a general sense. It is a specific fact about raindrop shape, not an investigation of factors affecting object movement.

copy.en:
Are raindrops really shaped like teardrops?

Nope! Small raindrops are almost perfectly round. Big ones flatten on the bottom like a tiny hamburger bun as they fall through the air!
copy.tl:
Hugis-luha ba talaga ang patak ng ulan?

Hindi! Ang maliliit na patak ay halos bilog. Ang malalaki naman ay pumapatag sa ilalim na parang munting pandesal habang bumabagsak sa hangin!
copy.bis:
Luha ba gyud ang porma sa tulo sa ulan?

Dili! Ang gagmay nga tulo halos lingin. Ang dagko mopatag sa ilawom morag gamay nga pan samtang nahulog sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We measure how much rain falls using millimeters (mm)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rain and its measurement unit, but does not teach identifying basic weather characteristics (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, cloud cover, etc.). It only gives a fact about rainfall measurement, which is tangential to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: using millimeters (mm)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions millimeters as a unit, but does not describe science process skills such as observing, predicting, or measuring in the context of simple science activities. It only notes that rainfall is measured in mm, without explaining the skill of measuring or its use in an activity.

copy.en: Did you know? We measure how much rain falls using millimeters (mm) — yep, the same tiny units you see on a ruler!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba? Sinusukat natin ang dami ng ulan gamit ang milimetro (mm) — yung maliit na units na nakikita mo sa ruler!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo? Ang gidaghanon sa ulan sukdon gamit ang milimetro (mm) — ang gagmay nga units nga imong makita sa ruler!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA uses colors! Yellow means be alert, orange means possible flooding, and red means serious flooding.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is specifically about Public Storm Warning Signals (PSWS) issued by PAGASA, which are numbered signals describing wind conditions. The card describes PAGASA rainfall warning colors (yellow/orange/red), a different warning system. It shares the PAGASA context but does not teach the PSWS conditions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA uses colors! Yellow means be alert, orange means possible flooding, and red means serious flooding.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires examining a local weather chart to interpret local weather and describing safety precautions for poor/extreme weather. The card explains the meaning of rainfall warning colors but does not involve a weather chart, local interpretation, or explicit safety precautions. It is related to weather warnings but does not directly support the chart-based interpretation or precaution practice.

copy.en:
How do we know if rain is dangerous?

PAGASA uses colors! Yellow means be alert, orange means possible flooding, and red means serious flooding. The redder it is, the more dangerous!
copy.tl:
Paano natin malalaman kung delikado ang ulan?

Gumagamit ang PAGASA ng kulay! Dilaw ay mag-ingat, orange ay posibleng baha, at pula ay delikadong baha. Mas pula, mas mapanganib!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagkahibalo kung delikado ang ulan?

Naggamit ang PAGASA og kolor! Dilaw mag-amping, orange mahimong mobaha, ug pula delikado nga baha. Kon mas pula, mas peligroso!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hot air rises, cools, and brings daily rain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes rising hot air and daily rain near the equator, which is a general convection/rainfall idea, but it does not mention solar energy, land and sea breezes, monsoons, or the ITCZ. It does not directly support the specific competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hot air rises, cools, and brings daily rain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rain but does not explain the water cycle or its role in the environment. It only notes that daily rain keeps the forest moist, which is a consequence, not an explanation of the water cycle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hot air rises, cools, and brings daily rain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes hot air rising and cooling, which is an atmospheric process, but it does not explicitly explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. The connection to solar energy is only implicit and not developed.

copy.en: Great tropical rainforests like the Amazon sit in a belt around the equator. Hot air rises, cools, and brings daily rain, keeping the forest always moist!
copy.tl: Ang mga tropical rainforest tulad ng Amazon ay nasa banda sa palibot ng equator. Ang mainit na hangin ay tumataas, lumalamig, at nagdadala ng araw-araw na ulan!
copy.bis: Ang mga tropical rainforest sama sa Amazon naa sa banda libot sa equator. Ang init nga hangin mosaka, mobugnaw, ug modala sa kada-adlaw nga ulan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The forest floor is the darkest layer of the rainforest, so only a few plants can grow there.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things for a group or class discussion and confirm and record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that darkness limits plant growth, which touches on the Sun's importance, but it does not involve making suggestions, class discussion, or confirming/recording ideas from secondary sources as the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The forest floor is the darkest layer of the rainforest, so only a few plants can grow there.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies light availability affects plant growth, but it does not identify basic needs such as air, food, water, and shelter, nor does it teach the basic needs of living things directly.

copy.en: The forest floor is the darkest layer of the rainforest, so only a few plants can grow there.
copy.tl: Ang sahig ng gubat ang pinakamadilim na bahagi ng rainforest, kaya kaunti lang ang halamang tumutubo doon.
copy.bis: Ang salog sa lasang mao ang labing ngitngit nga bahin sa rainforest, mao nga diyutay ra ang tanom nga motubo didto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cutting down forests could mean losing cures we haven't discovered yet
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a reason to conserve rainforests (to preserve potential medicines), but the competency is about protecting the environment so that living things can survive. The card does not address the survival of living things; it focuses on potential human medical benefits. This is related to conservation but does not directly teach the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many of the medicines we use today came from rainforest plants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining ecosystem stability during difficult conditions. The card mentions that rainforest plants provide medicines, implying biodiversity value, but it does not explain how biodiversity maintains stability during food shortages, disease, or climate change. It only touches on the value of undiscovered cures, which is not the same as ecosystem stability.

copy.en: Many of the medicines we use today came from rainforest plants — so cutting down forests could mean losing cures we haven't discovered yet.
copy.tl: Maraming gamot na ginagamit natin ngayon ay galing sa mga halaman ng rainforest — kaya kapag nawasak ang gubat, posibleng mawala rin ang mga posibleng gamot sa hinaharap.
copy.bis: Daghang tambal nga atong gigamit karon naggikan sa mga tanom sa rainforest — mao nga kung maguba ang lasang, mahimong mawala usab ang mga posibleng tambal sa umaabot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: saving fresh water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes rainwater harvesting as a way to save fresh water, which is a conservation practice. However, the competency requires recognizing the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive. The card does not explicitly connect water conservation to environmental protection or the survival of living things; it only mentions watering plants as a use. This is related to conservation but does not directly teach the stated competency.

copy.en:
What is rainwater harvesting?

In rainwater harvesting, rain running off a roof is collected in a barrel or tank to water plants or clean, saving fresh water!
copy.tl:
Ano ang rainwater harvesting?

Sa rainwater harvesting, ang tubig-ulan mula sa bubong ay iniimbak sa drum o tangke para sa pagdidilig o paglilinis, nakakatipid ng tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang rainwater harvesting?

Sa rainwater harvesting, ang tubig-ulan gikan sa atop tigumon sa drum o tangke aron magamit sa pagbisbis o paghugas, makadaginot og tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: raise it higher than the heart — this helps slow down the bleeding
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: First-aid raising a limb is not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: raise it higher than the heart — this helps slow down the bleeding
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: First-aid is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en: If a hand or leg is bleeding, raise it higher than the heart — this helps slow down the bleeding!
copy.tl: Kung nasusugatan ang kamay o paa, itaas ito nang mas mataas sa puso — makakatulong ito para bumagal ang pagdurugo!
copy.bis: Kung nasamad ang kamot o tiil, ipataas kini labaw sa kasingkasing — makatabang kini aron mohinay ang pagdugo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they hang together in clusters along the branches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Fruit clusters on branches are not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they hang together in clusters along the branches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: Fruit on branches is not observing the root and shoot system and why they are important.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rambutan fruits grow one by one, but they hang together in clusters
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Fruit clustering is morphology, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rambutan fruits grow one by one
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: One grow example is not grow, respond, and reproduce as general living-thing characteristics.

copy.en: Rambutan fruits grow one by one, but they hang together in clusters along the branches.
copy.tl: Ang rambutan ay tumutubo nang tig-iisa, pero nagsasama-sama ang mga ito sa kumpol sa sanga.
copy.bis: Ang rambutan motubo nga tag-usa, apan magtapok sila sa mga pungpong subay sa sanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sweet, juicy white flesh wrapped around a single seed inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Culinary flesh around a seed is fruit anatomy/food, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Crack open a rambutan and you'll find sweet, juicy white flesh wrapped around a single seed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Fruit flesh around a seed is not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

copy.en: Crack open a rambutan and you'll find sweet, juicy white flesh wrapped around a single seed inside.
copy.tl: Sa loob ng rambutan, may maputi at masarap na katas na balot sa iisang buto.
copy.bis: Sa sulod sa rambutan, adunay puti ug lami nga duga nga naglibot sa usa lang ka liso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sweet, juicy white flesh wrapped around the seed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Culinary flesh around a seed is fruit anatomy/food, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

copy.en: Inside a rambutan is sweet, juicy white flesh wrapped around the seed.
copy.tl: Sa loob ng rambutan ay may puti, makatas, at matamis na laman na nakabalot sa buto.
copy.bis: Sa sulod sa rambutan naay puti, tubigon, ug tam-is nga unod nga nagputos sa liso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The slope of a ramp shows how steep it is, measured by how much it rises compared to how far it runs out!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines the slope of a ramp (an inclined plane) but does not address the advantages or limitations of simple machines, nor does it involve a guided investigation. It only provides a definition of steepness, which is related vocabulary but not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: The slope of a ramp shows how steep it is, measured by how much it rises compared to how far it runs out!
copy.tl: Ang slope ng rampa ay kung gaano ito katarik, sinusukat sa kung gaano kataas ang inakyat kumpara sa kung gaano kahaba ang tinakbo nito!
copy.bis: Ang slope sa rampa mao ang pagkatarik niini, sukdon pinaagi sa gitas-on nga gisaka batok sa gilay-on nga gilakaw niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An eagle's eye has many more light-sensing cells than a human eye
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal body part (the eye) but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or gathering food. It is only broadly related to animal body parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An eagle's eye has many more light-sensing cells than a human eye
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sensory feature of an eagle but does not explain how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it give an example like mimicry or camouflage. It is only loosely related to adaptation.

copy.en:
How sharp is an eagle's eyesight?

An eagle's eye has many more light-sensing cells than a human eye, so it can spot far more detail than we can!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalinaw ang tanaw ng agila?

Mas marami ang mga selulang sumasagap ng liwanag sa mata ng agila kaysa sa tao, kaya mas marami itong detalyeng nakikita!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka klaro ang panan-aw sa agila?

Mas daghan ang mga selula nga modawat sa kahayag sa mata sa agila kay sa tawo, busa mas daghan og detalye ang makita niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rat's front teeth keep growing its whole life, so it gnaws on things to keep them from getting too long.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an outer body part (front teeth) but its described role is gnawing to control tooth length, not moving or gathering food as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rat's front teeth keep growing its whole life, so it gnaws on things to keep them from getting too long.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes continuous growth of teeth, which is a growth characteristic, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a set; it only gives a specific fact about one animal's teeth.

copy.en: A rat's front teeth keep growing its whole life, so it gnaws on things to keep them from getting too long.
copy.tl: Patuloy na tumutubo ang harapang ngipin ng daga habang buhay, kaya nginangatngat nila ang mga bagay para hindi ito lumaki nang sobra.
copy.bis: Padayon nga motubo ang atubangang ngipon sa ilaga samtang buhi, mao nga kutkuton niini ang mga butang aron dili motaas kaayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mother rat can give birth to about six to twelve pups in a single litter!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a rat gives birth to live pups, which is an example of a mammal giving birth to live young, but the competency requires identifying which groups of animals reproduce by live birth versus egg-laying. The card does not contrast groups or teach the classification skill; it only provides a specific litter-size fact.

copy.en:
How many babies can a rat have at once?

A mother rat can give birth to about six to twelve pups in a single litter!
copy.tl:
Ilang anak ang kayang ipanganak ng isang daga?

Ang isang inang daga ay maaaring manganak ng humigit-kumulang anim hanggang labindalawang anak sa isang pagsilang!
copy.bis:
Pila ka anak ang mahimong ipanganak sa usa ka ilaga?

Ang inahan nga ilaga makahimo og mga unom hangtod dose ka anak sa usa ka pagpanganak!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they need to keep their growing teeth short
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an outer body part (teeth) but describes their role as keeping teeth short, not as moving or gathering food as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they need to keep their growing teeth short
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral adaptation (gnawing) but does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment, nor does it use secondary sources or address mimicry/camouflage.

copy.en:
Why do rats gnaw on wires?

House rats and mice gnaw on wires and wood because they need to keep their growing teeth short.
copy.tl:
Bakit nginangatngat ng daga ang kable?

Ang mga daga sa bahay ay nangangagat ng kable at kahoy dahil kailangan nilang panatilihing maikli ang lumalaking ngipin.
copy.bis:
Ngano gikitkit sa ilaga ang alambre?

Ang mga ilaga sa balay mokitkit og alambre ug kahoy kay kinahanglan nilang mubo ang ilang nagatubo nga ngipon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: flat breastbone that lacks the strong muscles needed to power wings for flight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why ostriches and emus cannot fly by referring to a flat breastbone and lack of strong muscles. It does not describe outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement and food gathering, which is the focus of G3-L-4. The mention of wings is incidental and not used to teach their structure or function.

copy.en:
Why can't ostriches and emus fly?

These big birds have a flat breastbone that lacks the strong muscles needed to power wings for flight.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi makalipad ang ostrich at emu?

Ang malalaking ibong ito ay hindi makalipad dahil patag ang buto ng kanilang dibdib at walang malalakas na kalamnan para sa pakpak.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili makalupad ang ostrich ug emu?

Kining dagkong langgam dili makalupad tungod kay patag ang bukog sa ilang dughan ug walay kusog nga kaunoran para sa pako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water hyacinths have long roots that help the plant reach the soil under the water to get nutrients.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a plant root adaptation for obtaining nutrients; it does not address protecting or conserving the environment for living things to survive.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water hyacinths have long roots that help the plant reach the soil under the water to get nutrients.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant roots and nutrient uptake, not about proper handling and disposal of materials such as reusing, recycling, or disposing of waste.

copy.en: Water hyacinths have long roots that help the plant reach the soil under the water to get nutrients.
copy.tl: Ang water hyacinth ay may mahahabang ugat na tumutulong sa halaman na maabot ang lupa sa ilalim ng tubig upang makakuha ng nutrients.
copy.bis: Ang water hyacinth adunay tag-as nga mga gamot nga makatabang sa tanom nga maabot ang yuta ilawom sa tubig aron makakuha ug nutrients.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It helps you read food labels to see how much of a substance, like sugar or sodium, is in a product.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about using percentage composition to read food labels, which is a chemistry/mathematics concept. G4-F-4 requires constructing and labeling simple graphs of different speeds, which is entirely unrelated to food labels or percentage composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It helps you read food labels to see how much of a substance, like sugar or sodium, is in a product.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe uniform velocity and represent it using distance-time graphs
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses percentage composition in food labels, not uniform velocity or distance-time graphs. G7-F-7 is about describing uniform velocity and representing it with distance-time graphs, which has no connection to the card's content.

copy.en: How can percentage composition help you at the grocery store?\n\nIt helps you read food labels to see how much of a substance, like sugar or sodium, is in a product.
copy.tl:
Paano makakatulong ang percentage composition sa grocery store?

Nakakatulong ito para mabasa mo ang food labels at makita kung gaano karami ang isang substance, tulad ng asukal o sodium, sa isang produkto.
copy.bis:
Giunsa makatabang ang percentage composition sa grocery store?

Makatabang kini aron mabasa nimo ang food labels ug makita kung unsa ka daghan ang usa ka substance, sama sa asukal o sodium, sa usa ka produkto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It’s whoever hears the sound!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe and explain how sound changes when the source or the receiver are moving
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines who the receiver is in a sound context. It does not describe or explain how sound changes when the source or receiver are moving, which is the core action of G6-F-10. Defining the receiver is useful background but does not directly teach the Doppler-effect concept.

copy.en:
Who is the "receiver" in our sound lesson?

It’s whoever hears the sound! Like you standing on the sidewalk, not just a microphone on a stand.
copy.tl:
Sino ang "receiver" sa ating sound lesson?

Ito ay sinumang nakakarinig! Tulad mo sa bangketa, hindi lang mikropono sa patungan.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang "receiver" sa atong sound lesson?

Kinsa man nga makadungog! Sama nimo sa bangketa, dili lang mikropono sa patungan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A recessive trait only shows up when a child inherits two recessive alleles, one from each parent.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the fundamental rule for when a recessive trait is expressed, which is necessary background for constructing or interpreting family inheritance patterns. However, it does not itself represent patterns across generations of a family, so it does not directly teach the competency's action.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A recessive trait only shows up when a child inherits two recessive alleles, one from each parent.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict simple ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes in crosses involving dominant/recessive gene pairs
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the condition for recessive expression, which is needed to predict genotype/phenotype ratios in crosses. But it does not involve predicting ratios or performing crosses, so it only provides background knowledge rather than directly supporting the prediction skill.

copy.en:
When does a recessive trait show up?

A recessive trait only shows up when a child inherits two recessive alleles, one from each parent.
copy.tl:
Kailan lumalabas ang resesibong katangian?

Lalabas lang ang resesibong katangian kapag dalawang resesibong alelo ang taglay ng anak.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a mopakita ang resesibo nga kinaiya?

Mopakita lang ang resesibo nga kinaiya kon duha ka resesibo nga alelo ang naa sa anak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny charged particles called ions move from one side to the other when you use it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the internal ion movement in a rechargeable battery, but does not address assembling or drawing a simple circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb/motor/buzzer. The battery is only a component, not the circuit itself.
